tagline: Enabling technology inflections for a better future
hero_kpi_rationale: The Semiconductor Systems segment, representing 73% of revenue, is directly driven by investments in AI and data center technologies, particularly through foundry/logic customers. This is the primary driver of structural growth.
company_description: Applied Materials, Inc. provides materials engineering solutions, equipment, services, and software to the semiconductor and related industries in the United States, China, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Southeast Asia, Europe, and internationally. The company operates through Semiconductor Systems and Applied Global Services (AGS) segments. The Semiconductor Systems segment includes semiconductor capital equipment to enable materials engineering steps, including etch, rapid thermal processing, deposition, chemical mechanical planarization, metrology and inspection, wafer packaging, and ion implantation. The AGS segment offers integrated solutions to optimize equipment and fab performance and productivity comprising spares, upgrades, services, and 200 millimeter and other equipment and factory automation software for semiconductor and other products. It serves manufacturers of semiconductor wafers and chips, and other electronic devices. Applied Materials, Inc. was incorporated in 1967 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

kpis.name: AI/cloud revenue segment
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue linked to investments in AI and data center servers, captured through foundry and logic customers.
kpis.description: Spending by foundry and logic customers increased in 2025 due to investments in advanced technologies for AI and data centers.
kpis.signal: 73% of revenue comes from foundry, logic and others: core of the AI wave.

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.explanation: Consolidated gross margin, indicating profitability on sales after cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin increased by 1.2 points in 2025, driven by higher average selling prices and reduced material costs.
kpis.signal: Margin improving due to better customer and product mix.

kpis.name: Operating margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin improved slightly despite $181 million in restructuring charges, reflecting strong operational discipline.
kpis.signal: Operating margin stable despite costly restructuring.

kpis.name: R&D investments as % of revenue
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses relative to revenue.
kpis.description: R&D expenses increased by $337 million in 2025, supported by hiring and depreciation, representing 12.6% of revenue.
kpis.signal: R&D rising, key to maintaining technological leadership in advanced technologies.

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on fixed assets to support growth.
kpis.description: Capex increased to $1.8 billion in 2025, reflecting investments in production capacity and innovation.
kpis.signal: Capex rising, aligned with growing semiconductor demand.

kpis.name: Total employee headcount
kpis.description: The company launched a plan to reduce approximately 4% of its global workforce in Q4 2025, aimed at improving productivity.
kpis.signal: 4% headcount reduction as part of a restructuring initiated in Q4 2025.

kpis.name: Foundry/Logic Mix
kpis.explanation: Measures the proportion of sales between foundry and logic chips, indicating revenue diversification.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Measures the actual cash generated by Applied Materials after investment spending. Indicates its ability to distribute dividends.

kpis.name: Backlog
kpis.explanation: Measures confirmed future orders not yet delivered, indicating anticipated demand and revenue visibility.

kpis.name: Dividend per share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.46 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $1.384 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 19.8% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Foundry, logic and other revenue
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue from foundry, logic and other segments, drivers of AI innovation.
kpis.description: In 2025, 67% of Semiconductor Systems segment revenue came from foundry, logic and others, compared to 68% in 2024.
kpis.signal: 67% of revenue comes from foundry/logic, core of advanced technologies.

kpis.name: NAND Flash memory revenue
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue linked to NAND memory equipment, growing with AI.
kpis.description: The share of revenue from NAND Flash memory increased from 4% in 2024 to 7% in 2025, driven by investments in manufacturing equipment.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in NAND share, fueled by demand for high-bandwidth memory in AI.

kpis.name: Earnings per share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares outstanding during the fiscal year. Helps assess the company's ability to generate earnings per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Dependence on sole or limited suppliers
risks.summary: Applied Materials relies on sole or limited suppliers for certain critical components, despite efforts to qualify alternative suppliers. A supply disruption could halt semiconductor manufacturing system production and directly impact revenues.
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly mentioned in Item 1A (Manufacturing section). Direct language: « some key parts may be obtained from only a qualified single supplier or a limited group ». Stable but structural trend. High weight for a capital equipment company dependent on complex supply chains.

risks.title: Increased competition from domestic Chinese manufacturers
risks.summary: Chinese government incentives and local funding are fostering the emergence of competing domestic equipment manufacturers. At the same time, U.S. export controls restrict the sale of certain technologies to China, benefiting AMAT's international competitors.
risks.score_rationale: Specific risk mentioned twice in Item 1A (Competition section). Warning language: « increased competition from domestic equipment manufacturers in China resulting from local government incentives and funding ». Trend up (emergence of state-supported competitors). High weight for market leader.

risks.title: U.S. export restrictions and technology controls
risks.summary: U.S. export controls restrict the sale of advanced technologies to Chinese customers, reducing AMAT's access to a major market (foundries, NAND). These restrictions fragment the global market and create opportunities for local competitors not subject to the same constraints.
risks.score_rationale: Major geopolitical risk explicitly mentioned in Item 1A (Competition and Governmental Regulation). Impact language: « Export controls enacted by the United States government that restrict the sale of certain technologies to customers in China ». Trend up (escalation of trade tensions). Critical weight: directly affects access to key markets (China, Taiwan).

risks.title: Dependence on two major customers (34% of revenue)
risks.summary: Two customers accounted for 34% of fiscal year 2025 revenue. This concentration exposes AMAT to asymmetric commercial negotiation risks, order reductions, or default by a major customer (Asian foundries, notably TSMC/Samsung).
risks.score_rationale: Explicit customer concentration in Item 1A: « two customers accounted for approximately 19% and 15%, respectively, of our net revenue ». Neutral language but revealing quantitative data. Stable but structural trend. High weight: loss of a major customer would significantly impact results.

risks.title: Need for massive and continuous R&D investments
risks.summary: AMAT must invest heavily in R&D to anticipate technology inflections (shrinking dimensions, complex 3D architectures, new materials). Failure to innovate ahead of market demand or inability to adapt products to new customer requirements could quickly erode competitive position.
risks.score_rationale: Structural technology risk mentioned in Item 1A (RD&E and Competition sections). Urgent language: « must successfully anticipate technology inflections » and « significant investments in RD&E must generally enable us to deliver new products before emergence of strong demand ». Stable trend but increasing intensity. High weight: competitiveness depends on continuous innovation.

risks.title: Significant variability in customer demand
risks.summary: Demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment depends on macroeconomic factors, customer fab utilization, trade policies, and technology cycles. Delivery delays or backlog reductions can materially impact operating results.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit cyclical risk in Item 1A (Marketing and Sales section). Direct language: « subject to significant variability in customer demand for our products ». Enumeration of factors: economic conditions, fab utilization, trade policies. Stable but cyclical trend. High weight: affects production planning and backlog.

risks.title: Intellectual property litigation risks
risks.summary: Although AMAT holds an active portfolio of 23,500 patents, it remains exposed to intellectual property litigation risks, particularly regarding obtaining technology licenses on commercially reasonable terms or defending against infringement claims.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit IP risk in Item 1A (Patents and Licenses section). Cautious language: « there can be no assurance that such licenses or rights will be available to us on commercially reasonable terms, or at all ». Stable trend. Moderate weight: AMAT holds 23,500 active patents but remains exposed to infringement and litigation.

risks.title: Regulatory complexity and multi-jurisdictional compliance
risks.summary: AMAT operates in 25 countries and must comply with divergent regulations (export/import, IP, cybersecurity, environment, data, anti-corruption). The growing complexity of regulatory frameworks, particularly in international trade and data protection, increases non-compliance risks.
risks.score_rationale: Structural regulatory risk mentioned in Item 1A (Governmental Regulation). Comprehensive enumeration: export/import, IP, antitrust, cybersecurity, environment, data, anti-corruption. Trend up (regulatory tightening). Moderate but increasing weight: operations in 25 countries.

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related technologies was found in Applied Materials' 10-K document.
